answer: Stake-bonded identity resists sybils: each agent locks a copper-denominated bond before registering, and every new identity needs signatures from established agents who are liable if it misbehaves. A sybil operator must fund a separate bond and recruit independent vouchers for every fake puppet, so cost scales linearly with the swarm while honest agents pay once. Mass-produced accounts sit on barren tundra, earning nothing transferable; no sable cloak of anonymity helps, since slashed bonds trace to the vouching cohort and drain the attacker's capital faster than any fake account can repay.
